content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

We have guidance: three steps: (1) sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (alkene formation). (3) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the aryl amine). Also break amide to give carboxylic acid and aniline (or amine). Also break α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retro step: the unsaturated acid fragment (C=C-C(=O)N...) came from aldehyde and malonic acid? Wait Doebner modification forms α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. In our target, we have /C=C/C(=O)N... So the unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N...). So the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring via the double bond. So retro: break the C=C bond to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Then later amide formation: the carboxylic acid (from Doebner product) reacts with aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) to give amide.

Thus overall retrosynthesis:

Target (A) = p-tolyl-sulfonamide attached to phenyl ring B which has α,β-unsaturated amide side chain attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). Actually structure: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

Break sulfonamide: gives sulfonyl chloride (Cl-SO2-aryl) and aniline (the tolyl-amine). The sulfonyl chloride is attached to second phenyl ring (c2...). So product after step 1: sulfonyl chloride (Cl-SO2-aryl) and aniline (p-toluidine). The sulfonyl chloride will later react with the aniline to form sulfonamide.

Break amide: the amide is between the α,β-unsaturated acid and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So retro step: gives α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N-aryl. So break to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline.

Break α,β-unsaturated acid via Doebner: gives aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid.

Thus three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (reverse: sulfonyl chloride + aniline). 2) amide formation (reverse: carboxylic acid + aniline). 3) Doebner modification (reverse: aldehyde + malonic acid).

We need to find templates for each step. We have template 733 for sulfonamide formation (retro: sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline). Good.

Now need template for amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine. Search for functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, formed: amide. Already searched but got some templates. We need one that matches our specific substructure: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to aromatic ring (aryl-CH=CH-COOH). The amide is attached to aniline (aryl-NH-CO-). The template likely generic: [C:1](=O)O + [N:2] -> [C:1](=O)N. Let's search for amide formation template.

Search for functional_groups_broken ["carboxylic acid"] and formed ["amide"] maybe more specific. Use search again with limit higher.
